result.graft: From C: add one static 12-month average-burn headline to the burn card, with no segmented control, to give the chart a quantitative anchor.
result.defense: A is the only option solving both problems: it removes the dishonest control, makes scope explicit with 'Runway now', 'Cash today' and 'Monthly burn, 12 months', and prevents privacy leakage by masking Runway and flattening bars when amounts are hidden. It best serves the founder's quick-glance job with no interaction and least mock/data risk. B correctly scopes ranges to the burn card, but a header menu pill hides state, 30 daily bars are dense, three invented datasets risk inconsistent totals, and it says nothing about hidden amounts. C uses a familiar Stocks pattern, but its prominent segmented control still invites expectations that Runway/Cash will change, adds exploration the persona does not need, carries the same three-dataset effort/inconsistency risk, and also ignores the hidden-amounts decision.

result.graft: From B, keep the existing terse tile labels ('Runway' and 'Cash' rather than 'Runway now' and 'Cash today') to strictly honor the 'minimal copy (every word is UI)' rule, since both metrics are inherently point-in-time.
result.defense: Option A is the only proposal that solves both parts of the brief while respecting the founder persona and static-mockup constraints. Startup burn is lumpy within a month (payroll, rent, cloud bills), so the daily and weekly burn charts introduced by B and C create noisy, misleading signals just to justify keeping a broken control. Removing the range selector eliminates the false affordance where Runway and Cash never changed, keeps the 12-month monthly burn chart immediately glanceable on iPhone and Duo, and avoids drawing and maintaining three separate static placeholder datasets (which inflates effort and risk in B and C). Finally, only A resolves the undecided privacy requirement by masking Runway, flattening bar heights so relative burn spikes do not leak in the hidden state, and placing the Hide amounts eye cleanly at the top of the Desk layout.
